questions.q: What does a market order guarantee?
options: A specific execution price
Execution, but not a specific price
Both execution and price
Neither execution nor price
questions.explain: A market order fills immediately against the best available resting orders — it guarantees the trade happens, not at what exact price.

questions.q: A trader places a limit order to buy at $49.50 when the stock is trading at $50.00. What happens if the price never falls to $49.50?
options: The order automatically converts to a market order after one hour
The order is canceled immediately
The order simply rests, unfilled, on the limit order book
The exchange fills it anyway at $50.00
questions.explain: A limit order guarantees price, not execution. If the market never reaches the limit price, the order just sits unfilled on the book.

questions.q: On the limit order book, how is the bid side ranked?
options: Lowest price first
Highest price first
By order size, largest first
Randomly, to prevent front-running
questions.explain: The bid side holds resting buy orders ranked from highest (most aggressive) price down to lowest.

questions.q: Two buy limit orders are both priced at $50.00. Order A arrived at 9:30:01 AM and Order B arrived at 9:30:05 AM. Under price-time priority, which fills first when a matching sell order arrives?
options: Order B, because it is the most recent
Order A, because it arrived first at the same price
They fill simultaneously and split the trade evenly
Whichever order is larger in size always fills first
questions.explain: Price-time priority fills better prices first; when prices tie, the order that arrived earliest is filled first.

questions.q: What does the NBBO (National Best Bid and Offer) represent?
options: The average bid and ask price over the past trading day
The best bid and ask available at a single, designated primary exchange only
The single best bid and best ask price available across all trading venues combined
A regulatory ceiling on how wide the bid-ask spread can be
questions.explain: The NBBO aggregates quotes across all competing venues (exchanges, ECNs, etc.) to identify the single best bid and best ask available anywhere.
